To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the three-valued logic K-T can be used for reasoning with incomplete data in a KBS; (ii) the proof method can be used to prove the consistency of a knowledge base (KB) and also to derive answers to queries; (iii) the proof method is sound, complete and decidable; (iv) an algorithm has been developed for computing the three values of the logic; (v) an implementation of the logic has been developed in Prolog and tested; and

(1) we have developed a computational model for answering questions in a KBS; (2) the model has been implemented as a prototype system; (3) the model has a three-valued semantics and a proof method; and (4) the model has the capability of dealing with incomplete information.

a computational model for reasoning about partiality and modality.
the problem of providing helpful answers to questions in a KBS.
the following: How to provide helpful answers to questions posed in a natural language in KBSs?
